items.name: waitUntil
items.title: waitUntil
items.description:
Suspends execution of scheduled script until the given condition satisfied.
- This command will loop and call the code inside `{}` **mostly every frame**, depends on complexity of the condition and the overall engine load, until the code returns true
- If the very first execution of the code returns true the command will exit immediately, therefore it will not produce any "Suspending not allowed in this context" error when used inside non-scheduled script. For all other uses it must be executed in environment that allows suspension (canSuspend), such as spawned or execVMed code
- Avoid doing `waitUntil { time > 20 };` and use `sleep 20;` instead!
- If you can, add a sleep to the condition to save some cpu cycles `waitUntil { sleep 1; !alive player };`

> [!NOTE]
> **Arma 3:** Since Arma 3 v1.94, a *condition* returning anything other than true or false **will** result in an appropriate type error.

params.name: condition
params.description: the expression that **must** return a Boolean, true to finish waiting or false to continue waiting
params.text: condition: Code - the expression that **must** return a Boolean, true to finish waiting or false to continue waiting

returns.description: the value the condition evaluates to when the wait is over (normally true)
returns.text: Anything - the value the condition evaluates to when the wait is over (normally true)

params.description: the expression that **must** return a Boolean, true to finish waiting or false to continue waiting
params.text: condition: Code - the expression that **must** return a Boolean, true to finish waiting or false to continue waiting

params.name: timeout
params.description: a timeout in seconds of game time (sleep vs uiSleep). The timeout is only checked after the condition was checked. **Any negative value disables the timeout**
params.text: timeout: Number - a timeout in seconds of game time (sleep vs uiSleep). The timeout is only checked after the condition was checked. **Any negative value disables the timeout**

params.name: interval
params.description: the time interval in seconds of game time between condition checks, this is equivalent to using a "sleep" after the condition.
params.text: interval: Number - (Optional, default 0) the time interval in seconds of game time between condition checks, this is equivalent to using a "sleep" after the condition.

returns.description: the value the condition evaluates to when the wait is over (normally true), or Nothing if the timeout ended the wait
returns.text: Anything - the value the condition evaluates to when the wait is over (normally true), or Nothing if the timeout ended the wait

params.name: scriptHandle
params.description: a script handle or promise to wait on
params.text: scriptHandle: Script Handle - a script handle or promise to wait on

returns.description: The result of the script or Promise
returns.text: Anything - The result of the script or Promise

params.name: scriptHandle
params.description: a script handle or promise to wait on
params.text: scriptHandle: Script Handle - a script handle or promise to wait on

returns.description: the result of the script or Promise. Or Nothing if timed out.
returns.text: Anything - the result of the script or Promise. Or Nothing if timed out.

examples.text:
waitUntil can lead to performance loss if used improperly:

```sqf
waitUntil { not alive player };            // bad
waitUntil { sleep 1; not alive player };    // good - checks every 1 second
player addEventHandler ["Killed", {  }];    // best - don't forget about Event Handlers
```
code:
waitUntil { not alive player };			// bad
waitUntil { sleep 1; not alive player };	// good - checks every 1 second
player addEventHandler ["Killed", {  }];	// best - don't forget about Event Handlers

waitUntil { bank getVariable ["money", 0] > 0 };
waitUntil { missionNamespace getVariable ["isready", false] };

examples.text:
Always return Boolean:

```sqf
waitUntil { sleep 1; if (not alive player) exitWith {}; _time = _time + 1 };                // bad
waitUntil { sleep 1; if (not alive player) exitWith { true }; _time = _time + 1; false };    // good
waitUntil { sleep 1; not alive player };                                                    // perfect
```
code:
waitUntil { sleep 1; if (not alive player) exitWith {}; _time = _time + 1 };				// bad
waitUntil { sleep 1; if (not alive player) exitWith { true }; _time = _time + 1; false };	// good
waitUntil { sleep 1; not alive player };													// perfect

items.problems:
For some unknown reason if you have waitUntil loop active and game is **saved/loaded**, some variables in the expression may appear undefined for a short time. As a workaround, assign expression to a variable and make sure it is defined before waitUntil checks it:

```sqf
waitUntil { private _expression = someBooleanVar && (someNumberVar > 10); !isNil "_expression" && { _expression } };
```

notes.text: waitUntil suspends both SQF functions and SQF scripts. In functions, the calling script is still in suspension due to waiting for a return from the call command. The game engine will continue, however. See Function for more detail.

Prior to Arma 3 v1.94 if waitUntil uses an undefined call code, waitUntil won't release, even when this code is separated from other conditions through or. Be warned that this won't cause an error message.

items.name: weaponsItems
items.title: weaponsItems
items.description:
Returns an array with subarrays contains class names and also names of connected items of all the vehicle's weapons.

> [!NOTE]
> This command can return weapon magazine(s) if any are present. Or an empty array if weapon is stored without a magazine in it.

- Arma 3 v1.22 it is possible to query weapon holders and ammo crates with this command.
If the argument is a vehicle, the command will return vehicle's weapons.
If the argument is a container, the command will act identical to weaponsItemsCargo.
- Arma 3 v1.96 the returned array always contains secondary muzzle magazine info and consistent with getUnitLoadout format for weapon items.
- Arma 3 v2.02 the returned array can contains binocular weapon items.

items.name: while
items.title: while
items.description:
Repeats Code while the given condition is true. A part of while-do construct.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - A while loop does not have any suspension, meaning that if used in scheduled environment without any suspension (sleep or uiSleep) the code will run multiple times per frame and consumes the 3 ms per frame scheduler execution limit. This should be avoided if not intended (see #Example 3).
> - In non-scheduled environment, while do loop is limited to 10,000 iterations, after which it exits even if condition is still true.

code: while { a < b } do { a = a + 1 };

notes.text:
The boolean code that is used to evaluate the while condition can be preceded by code that executes a regular command.

```sqf
while { _a =_a + 1; _a < 10 } do { /* ... */ };
```

items.name: with
items.title: with
items.description:
Creates a With Type that is used inside a do construct in order to execute code inside a given namespace.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> To avoid the below-mentioned issue error (whether in scheduled or unscheduled environment) use setVariable/getVariable with the desired Namespace.
items.problems:
When used in a do-construct in scripts with allowed suspension, a namespace switching might unexpectedly occur inside some scopes (for, if, try, call) started in a scheduled environment after small suspension if with was not the main scope; however, the issue does not arise if with is used in the parent scope: | namespace switch risk | namespace switch safe | |---|---| | ```sqf
0 spawn
{
with uiNamespace do
{
for "_i" from 1 to 1 do
{
systemChat str [
currentNamespace isEqualTo uiNamespace,
currentNamespace isEqualTo missionNamespace
];
// result [true, false]
sleep 0.05; // <-- small suspension
systemChat str [
currentNamespace isEqualTo uiNamespace,
currentNamespace isEqualTo missionNamespace
];
// result [false, true] <-- switching
};
};
};
``` | ```sqf
with uiNamespace do
{
0 spawn
{
for "_i" from 1 to 1 do
{
systemChat str [
currentNamespace isEqualTo uiNamespace,
currentNamespace isEqualTo missionNamespace
];
// result [true, false]
sleep 0.05; // <-- small suspension
systemChat str [
currentNamespace isEqualTo uiNamespace,
currentNamespace isEqualTo missionNamespace
];
// result [true, false] <-- NO switching
};
};
};
``` |
